_note: Northstar's classification, as data. Compiled by packs.declarative against the closed signal registry in packs.signals. Rung order is load-bearing: contra_invoice sits ABOVE invoice_with_attachment because Federal Recycling is a single-page contra and Complete Beverage is a multi-page invoice that also contains negative lines. Testing 'has attachments' first would misclassify any multi-page invoice with a rebate line; testing 'has negatives' first would misclassify Complete Beverage.

rungs.name: credit_memo_title
rungs._why: A genuine TITLE near the top of page 1. Length alone cannot separate it from a footnote: real OCR of Complete Beverage's 'For remaining credited items refer to Credit memo 32684.' wraps onto SHORT lines at index 25-26, while the real title on _AP Invoice 32473 sits at index 5. max_line_index 10 is wide enough to keep index 5 with room to spare and well short of 25.

rungs.name: all_commodity_rates_negative
rungs._why: Every per-unit RATE is negative. The /UNIT suffix is what makes it a rate rather than an amount: U-PAK prints -40.500 and Complete Beverage -0.65, both negative unit prices with no suffix, and neither is a contra.

rungs.name: one_primary_plus_supporting
rungs._why: An invoice with something stapled behind it - unless the pages share an N OF M footer, which proves they are one continuous invoice rather than an attachment.

rungs.name: statement_title_no_table
rungs._why: A document with a payable amount and service line items is a bill, whatever its header says - so the charges table has to be ABSENT.

rungs.name: northstar_letterhead
rungs._why: First few lines only. Every corpus document names Northstar somewhere - it is the bill-to on all six - so a whole-page search would call every one own paperwork.

tags._why: A standalone banner OR an aging header corroborated by a nonzero 30/60/90 bucket. primary_only is false DELIBERATELY: Federal Recycling's terms-and-conditions page is a supporting page. Pinned by test_a_past_due_banner_on_a_supporting_page_still_tags.
The column LABEL is printed on every Veritiv invoice, taxed or not. Only a real value separates them.

Supporting pages only. Federal Recycling carries a handwritten margin note OCR transcribes, but it is single-page with no supporting page and is correctly untagged. Threshold measured on the corpus: Complete Beverage's handwritten BOL pages score 0.51 and 0.46, its printed invoice and certificate pages 0.22 and 0.28, Federal Recycling's printed page 0.17. 0.40 sits in the gap with room on both sides.

claim._why: This pack is an AP department: every invoice it handles is billed TO Northstar, so the guard is the bill-to. Precision measured for the first time on 2026-08-07 - before tightening, the pack claimed an unrelated vendor's invoice billed to a different company at the marker ZIP, and one billed to a company in Austin whose only tie was a SHIP-TO block.

rules._why: Each names the company, or an address specific enough that no other business prints it. The PO Box appears without the company name at all on the EDCO remittance stub.

The bare ZIP was added so 4 real EDCO invoices with typo'd company names (NORTHSTART, NORTHSTRAY, NORTHSTAR RECY) would still be claimed - but a bare ZIP claims any document printing it. `northst` is the longest prefix every real rendering shares; measured, 28 of 28 real EDCO samples carry it, including all 4 that depend on the ZIP.

vetoes._why: Goods can be delivered here on an invoice billed to somebody else. Measured across all 111 second-samples: 100 documents carry a marker on a primary-page line and for ZERO of them is every such line a ship-to line, so this costs nothing real.
